t: You're looking at John Trundle Court, a mid-rise terrace block on the Barbican Estate. It takes its name from John Trundle, who lived from 1575 to 1629 and was a London publisher and bookseller. That's the link here: the block is named in his memory, as a nod to the city's old book trade. The material I have doesn't say more about his shop or what he printed, so I'll leave it there. It's a quiet corner of the estate, worth a slow look at the terraced form.
